statement: The exact cohomological dimensions and the real exception — Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated of transcendence degree $n$, let $k$ be the algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$ in $K$, and put $P=G_{K\overline k}$ and $E=G_K$. With continuous cohomology of discrete torsion modules, \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell P=n\quad\hbox{for every prime }\ell, \qquad \operatorname{cd}P=n, \] \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell E=n+2\quad(\ell\ne2),\qquad \operatorname{cd}_2E= \begin{cases}n+2&K\text{ not formally real},\\ \infty&K\text{ formally real}. \end{cases} \] In every case $\operatorname{vcd}_2E=\operatorname{cd}_2G_{K(i)}=n+2$. Thus the equalities proposed in F1 hold, with precisely this exception at two (149, section 1, manuscript p.~6, scan 13). For a general function field, the relevant condition is an ordering of $K$ itself, not just a real embedding of its constant number field.

statement: Finite-order elements and complex conjugation — For a field $F$ of characteristic zero, every nonidentity element of finite order in $G_F=\operatorname{Gal}(F^{\rm sep}/F)$ has order two. Its centralizer is the subgroup of order two that it generates. In $G_{\mathbb Q}$ all such elements are conjugate to the complex conjugation determined by $\overline{\mathbb Q}\subset\mathbb C$. Every open subgroup of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ has trivial centralizer in $G_{\mathbb Q}$. This answers F2 (149, section 1, manuscript p.~6, scan 14).

statement: Open subgroups, torsion, and centers of profinite surface groups — Let $P$ be the full profinite completion of either a free group of finite rank $r\geq2$, or the fundamental group of a closed oriented surface of genus $g\geq2$. Every open subgroup has trivial centralizer in $P$, and $P$ has no nonidentity element of finite order. An open subgroup of index $d$ is the full profinite completion of a free group of rank $1+d(r-1)$, respectively a surface group of genus $1+d(g-1)$. The free rank-one exception is $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$, whose center and the centralizers of all its open subgroups equal the whole group. These statements answer F3 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~7 and 13, scans 15 and 28).

statement: The rational-point group of a semiabelian variety — Let $K$ be finitely generated over its prime field and let $1\to T\to G\to A\to1$ be a semiabelian variety over $K$. statement: Corollaries 1(b), 2(c)--(d), and 3 with all comparison maps — A hyperbolic polycurve means a finite tower of smooth pairs whose geometric curve fibres have $2g-2+r>0$, including proper fibres. Over a field finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$, rational points of a hyperbolic polycurve have distinct geometric conjugacy classes of full point sections, and a point section has trivial centralizer in the geometric group. For a reduced geometrically connected finite-type source, the arithmetic outer fundamental-group map therefore determines a morphism into that polycurve. The same morphism rigidity holds for a target immersed in a semiabelian variety, already after geometrically abelianizing both extensions. Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, two maps $f,g:X\to Y$ with equal geometric outer maps are equal in each of these cases: $Y$ is a hyperbolic polycurve and $f$ has open image on fundamental groups; or $Y$ is immersed in a semiabelian variety and $C_{\pi_1(Y)}(f_*\pi_1(X))=1$. In particular a dominant map from an irreducible reduced source into a hyperbolic polycurve is rigid in this sense. These are Corollaries 1(b), 2(c)--(d), and 3 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~11--15, scans 24--31; F5).

statement: The Hartogs extension of a rational section — \textup{[F11; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 32, 34--35, 41; scans 65, 70--72, 83.]} Let $S$ be a smooth integral scheme of finite type over a field of characteristic zero. For a closed subset $Z\subset S$ of codimension at least two, restriction is a bijection \[ \operatorname{Sect}_S(U)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Sect}_{S\setminus Z}(U\times_S(S\setminus Z)). \] The same assertion holds for a finite tower of such relative curves.

statement: The trait criterion, including the two nonhyperbolic types — \textup{[F12; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 36--38; scans 74--78.]} Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $K$ its fraction field, and let $U=\bar U\setminus D$ be a smooth pair over $R$ of type other than $(0,0),(0,1)$. Let $f_K\in U(K)$. In characteristic zero for the residue field use all geometric covers; in residue characteristic $p>0$ use the geometrically pro-prime-to-$p$ fundamental groups. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $f_K$ extends to an $R$-section of $U$; \item the continuous lift $G_K\to E_U^{(p')}$ induced by $f_K$ factors through $\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}R)$; \item this lift is trivial on an inertia group at the closed point. \end{enumerate} Here ``factors'' means that the induced map on the quotient is a section of $E_U^{(p')}\to\pi_1(R)$. For nonhenselian $R$, inertia is taken in a chosen decomposition group, and its closed normal closure is the kernel of $G_K\to\pi_1(R)$. The statement extends to a tower of smooth pairs whose curve factors have these types.

statement: The nonabelian intersection formula and the five conditions — \textup{[F12; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 37--39 and 44; scans 75--79, 90.]} Let $R$ be henselian and use the notation of C2. Suppose that the proper extension of $f_K$ meets a rational cusp $q$ in the closed fibre. If $z$ is a local equation of $q$ and $t$ a uniformizer of $R$, write \[ f_K^*z=t^\mu u,\qquad u\in R^*,\qquad \mu>0. \] With positive Kummer inertia defined by $\tau\mapsto\tau(z^{1/n})/z^{1/n}$, the induced continuous homomorphism on inertia is, up to the geometric conjugation arising from the chosen path, \[ I_K\longrightarrow I_K/P_K=T_{p'} \xrightarrow{[\mu]}T_{p'}\xrightarrow{\kappa_q}\Pi^{(p')}. \tag{C.1} \] For $p=0$, $P_K=1$. The formula holds with one cusp. With at least two cusps it induces on the toric part of homology \[ T_\ell\longrightarrow T_\ell^{D(\bar k)}/T_\ell, \qquad a\longmapsto\mu a e_q \pmod{T_\ell\cdot(1,\ldots,1)}. \tag{C.2} \] In equicharacteristic zero, the five conditions a)--e) of scan 90 are equivalent for the lift $\lambda:G_K\to E_U$: injectivity of $\lambda$; the positive-multiplicity formula (C.1); nontrivial inertia; failure of descent to $\pi_1(R)$; and failure of $f_K$ to extend into $U$. In that case its image has index $\mu$ in the cusp normalizer. For $p>0$, replace the domain in the injectivity assertion by $G_K/P_K$, and replace the index by $\mu_{p'}=\prod_{\ell\ne p}\ell^{v_\ell(\mu)}$.

If $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Out}(\Pi)$ is its continuous outer action, the continuous map \[ E\longrightarrow E_\rho=\{(a,g)\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Pi)\times G: [a]=\rho(g)\},\qquad e\longmapsto(\operatorname{conj}_e,\bar e) \tag{C.4} \] is an isomorphism. statement: The normalizer extension and its sign — \textup{[F14; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 39--41; scans 79--82.]} Assume the hyperbolic case of C4 and let $q:S\to D$ be a boundary section. Put $M=I_q/I_q^2$ and $N=M^\vee=q^*\mathcal O_{\bar U}(q)$. For a chosen peripheral subgroup $L_q=\kappa_q(T)\subset\Pi$, the normalizer $N_E(L_q)$ fits in an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow T\longrightarrow N_E(L_q) \longrightarrow G\longrightarrow1. \tag{C.5} \] With the positive Kummer inertia convention of C3 its extension class is $c_1(N)$, and hence is $-c_1(M)$. More precisely, its image in $H^2(G,\mu_n)$ corresponds under the comparison map to the Kummer class of $N$ in $H^2(S,\mu_n)$; when $S$ is an \'etale $K(\pi,1)$ this comparison is an isomorphism. For type $(0,2)$ the same conclusion holds whenever the exact sequence of C4 holds (in particular over the arithmetic $K(\pi,1)$ bases of C7): here $L_q=\Pi=T$, its arithmetic normalizer is all of $E$, and the two distinguished boundary sections identify $U$ with the punctured normal line $N^\times$. Type $(1,0)$ has no cusp, so no normalizer extension of this kind is asserted there.

statement: The arithmetic splitting and completed-unit criteria — \textup{[F14--F15; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 40--42; scans 81--82, 85.]} Let $S$ be smooth connected of finite type over a field finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$, and suppose that $S$ is an \'etale $K(\pi,1)$. Then $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ is finitely generated, the integral continuous comparison in degree two is an isomorphism \[ H^2(G,T)\simeq H^2(S,T), \] and Kummer theory gives \[ H^1(G,T)\simeq H^1(S,T) \simeq\widehat{\mathcal O(S)^*} :=\varprojlim_n\mathcal O(S)^*/\mathcal O(S)^{*n}. \tag{C.6} \] For the boundary section of C6, (C.5) splits if and only if $M$, equivalently $N$, is a trivial line bundle. A global basis of $M$ is sufficient over any characteristic-zero base for which (C.5) exists. Here a ``uniformizer along $q$'' means a basis of $I_q/I_q^2$; the statement does not require a global equation of $q$ on an entire neighborhood of its image.

statement: The geometric torsor inside the completed torsor — \textup{[F15; \S3, manuscript p.\ 42; scan 85.]} Under the arithmetic hypotheses of C7, $\mathcal O(S)^*$ contains no nonidentity element divisible by every positive integer in that group. The completion map in (C.6) is injective. When $N$ is trivial, the set of its nowhere-zero sections is a torsor under $\mathcal O(S)^*$. Its tangential splittings inject into the set of $T$-conjugacy classes of splittings of (C.5), a torsor under $H^1(G,T)$. Under these actions the map of torsors is induced by the injective Kummer map \[ \mathcal O(S)^*\hookrightarrow\widehat{\mathcal O(S)^*}. \] For bases of the conormal line, rather than normal vectors, multiplying the basis by $a$ changes this Kummer class by $-\kappa(a)$.

statement: Divisorial failure of extension and tangential specialization — \textup{[F16; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 46--47; scans 93--95.]} Let $S$ be smooth integral in characteristic zero and let $f_K$ be a rational section of a smooth pair as in C1. Let $S'$ be its maximal open domain as a section of $U$. Every irreducible component of $S\setminus S'$ has codimension one. At the generic point of such a component $D_\alpha$, the proper extension meets a unique cusp, and \[ \mu_\alpha=\operatorname{ord}_{D_\alpha}(f_K^*z)>0 \] is its intersection multiplicity, independent of a unit multiple of the local cusp equation $z$. The sum $\sum_\alpha\mu_\alpha D_\alpha$ is an effective Cartier divisor because $S$ is regular. On an open subset $W$ of the regular locus of $D_\alpha$ where the compactified section and the cusp are defined, and where a uniformizer $t$ of $D_\alpha$ has been fixed, write $z\circ f=t^{\mu_\alpha}u$ with $u$ regular and invertible along $W$. The resulting conormal isomorphism is \[ f_W^*(I_q/I_q^2)\xrightarrow{\sim} (I_{D_\alpha}/I_{D_\alpha}^2)^{\otimes\mu_\alpha}, \qquad z\longmapsto u\,t^{\mu_\alpha}. \tag{C.7} \] It produces tangential specialization of the geometric section at every point of $W$, compatible with specialization inside $W$. Changing $t$ to $at$ replaces the leading coefficient by $a^{-\mu_\alpha}u$, and changes the associated Kummer class by $-\mu_\alpha\kappa(a)$ in the scalar-coordinate convention.

statement: Inertia, its ranks, and a splitting (F22) — For every valuation $v$ of $L/K$ there are a continuous exact sequence and a canonical pairing \[ 1\longrightarrow I_v\longrightarrow D_v\longrightarrow G_{\kappa(v)}\longrightarrow1, \qquad I_v\simeq\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\Gamma_v\otimes\mathbb Q/\Gamma_v,\mu_\infty\bigr) \simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma_v,T). \] The sequence has a continuous splitting, with no canonical choice. The conjugation action on inertia is the cyclotomic action on the values in $T$. More precisely, \[ I_v\simeq\prod_{\ell}\mathbb Z_\ell(1)^{r_\ell},\qquad r_\ell=\dim_{\mathbb F_\ell}(\Gamma_v/\ell\Gamma_v) \le\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\Gamma_v\otimes\mathbb Q) \le\operatorname{trdeg}_K L-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(v). \] The product decomposition is noncanonical. Neither the manuscript codimension nor, in general, the rational rank determines the inertia group. In particular $\Gamma_v=\mathbb Q$ gives $I_v=1$, and $\Gamma_v=\mathbb Z[1/2]$ gives $I_v=\prod_{\ell\ne2}\mathbb Z_\ell(1)$. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~61, scan 124, ``des $T_\infty^\alpha$ essentiellement'' and ``scinder''.

statement: The exact inertia normalizer for arbitrary valuations (F19) — Let $I_v\ne1$. Let $\Delta_v$ be the largest divisible convex subgroup of the ordered group $\Gamma_v$, and let $w$ be the coarsening with value group $\Gamma_v/\Delta_v$, with its prolongation induced by $\overline v$. Then \[ I_w=I_v,\qquad N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_w, \qquad N_{P_{L/K}}(I_v)=D_w\cap P_{L/K}. \] There is an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow I_v\longrightarrow N_{P_{L/K}}(I_v) \longrightarrow G_{\kappa(w)\overline K}\longrightarrow1. \] Here $\kappa(w)\overline K$ is the compositum inside the residue algebraic closure induced by $\overline v$. Consequently geometric self-normalization holds precisely when that compositum is separably closed. The arithmetic identity $N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_v$ holds precisely when the induced residual valuation $v/w$ is henselian on $\kappa(w)$. It holds in particular for every rank-one valuation with nontrivial inertia, including every DVR. For $I_v=1$ the inertia normalizer is all of $G_L$. \par\emph{Passages:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~59 and 63, scans 119--120 and 127.

statement: The image of an arbitrary valuation at a crossing (F25, 2$^\circ$) — Let a valuation $v$ have center $x$ on $X$, let the branches through $x$ have parameters $z_1,\ldots,z_r$, and put $\gamma_i=v(z_i)$. The homomorphism from valuation inertia to the local geometric group is \[ \rho_v:\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma_v,T)\longrightarrow T^r, \qquad \chi\longmapsto(\chi(\gamma_1),\ldots,\chi(\gamma_r)). \] It is dual to the homomorphism of discrete torsion groups \[ \psi_v:\mathbb Q^r/\mathbb Z^r\longrightarrow (\Gamma_v\otimes\mathbb Q)/\Gamma_v, \qquad (q_i)\longmapsto\sum_iq_i\gamma_i\pmod{\Gamma_v}. \] Consequently $\operatorname{im}\rho_v$ is open exactly when $\ker\psi_v$ is finite, and it is all of $T^r$ exactly when $\ker\psi_v=0$. More explicitly, openness requires rational independence of the $\gamma_i$. Under that independence, with $\Lambda=\sum_i\mathbb Z\gamma_i$, \[ \ker\psi_v=(\Gamma_v\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{\gamma_i\})/\Lambda. \] Thus openness is exactly finite saturation index, and surjectivity is exactly equality of this saturation with $\Lambda$. Equality of rational rank and number of branches alone is insufficient. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~64--65, scans 130--131, 2$^\circ$ and the monomial example (36).

statement: The precise criterion for the stratum extension (F26) — Work first over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. For a nonempty connected open stratum \[ S=D_J^\circ=\Bigl(\bigcap_{j\in J}D_j\Bigr)\setminus\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\notin J}D_i\Bigr), \qquad L_j=N_{D_j/X}|_S, \] let $P=\prod_{j\in J,S}L_j^\times$ be the product of the punctured normal line bundles. Its fundamental groups have the exact homotopy sequence \[ \pi_2^{\mathrm{et}}(S)\xrightarrow{\partial}T^J \longrightarrow\pi_1(P)\longrightarrow\pi_1(S)\longrightarrow1. \] The same sequence computes the punctured tubular neighborhood of this stratum. With positive fiber meridians and the clutching convention specified below, \[ \partial(a)=\bigl(\langle c_1(L_j),a\rangle\bigr)_{j\in J}. \] In particular (37) is left exact precisely when these Chern evaluations vanish. An equivalent criterion, involving only finite covers and line bundles, is: for every positive integer $n$ there is a connected finite \emph{\'etale} cover $S'\to S$ such that every $L_j|_{S'}$ is an $n$th tensor power in $\operatorname{Pic}(S')$. Vanishing of $\pi_2^{\mathrm{et}}(S)$ suffices, but is not necessary. Over a nonclosed field the same assertion descends with the cyclotomic action and the permutation of geometric branch labels. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~66--67, scans 133--135, (37) and its qualification.

statement: Continuous semilinear actions descend to a finite quotient over the base field — \textup{[\S3, manuscript pp.\ 29--33; scans 58--59, 62--63, 66--67.]} Let $k$ have characteristic zero. A continuous section of $E_U\to G_k$ for a hyperbolic curve $U/k$ defines a semilinear action on its universal geometric pro-cover, equivariant for the ordinary scalar action on $U_{\bar k}$. These are exactly the continuous semilinear actions equivariant for that specified projection. More generally, let $\mathcal U$ be the universal pro-cover of a hyperbolic curve over $\bar k$, and let $\Omega$ be the union of the function fields of its finite covering levels. Give the semilinear automorphism group the topology of pointwise convergence on the discrete field $\Omega$. Every semilinear $G_k$-action for which each $f\in\Omega$ has open stabilizer admits a finite hyperbolic quotient $W/k$: there is an equivariant projection $\mathcal U\to W_{\bar k}$, its deck group is normalized by all of $G_k$, and the action comes from a continuous section of $E_W\to G_k$. The geometric quotient can be chosen as a finite \'etale cover of any prescribed initial level. Consequently the family of Conjecture B with the $G_k^\circ$ strengthening of scan 61, and that of Conjecture B' at the same field $k$, each quantified over all hyperbolic curves and with this continuity clause in B', are equivalent. This statement uses $G_k^\circ$-fixed compatible geometric pro-points on both sides. Every semilinear automorphism also extends canonically to the completed pro-cover. The natural $G_k$-action on germs of geometric-conjugacy classes of sections is well defined; the point-section map to those germs is equivariant and injective for $k$ finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$.
